speaker: patient
caregiver
doctor
documents.purpose: Use only facts explicitly spoken in the consultation transcript. Never add information that was not said.
include: Exact numbers and units as spoken
examples: Fever for two days remains fever for two days.
counterexamples: Do not diagnose viral fever from fever alone.
Do not write blood pressure 120/80 when it was not said.

speaker: patient
caregiver
doctor
documents.purpose: Route facts to SOAP sections based on who supplied the information, never on what the system infers.
include: Patient or caregiver reports of symptoms, history, and concerns go to Subjective
Measured or clinically observed facts go to Objective
Doctor diagnostic opinions and assessments go to Assessment
Doctor orders, prescriptions, and advice go to Plan
exclude: Doctor questions treated as patient answers
Patient guesses or self-diagnoses treated as doctor assessments
examples: Doctor: Are you taking tablets? is a question, not current medication.
Patient: I think it might be dengue is patient speculation, not Assessment.
counterexamples: Do not treat a medicine named only in a doctor question as patient history.
Do not route patient speculation to assessment.

speaker: patient
caregiver
doctor
documents.purpose: Leave undiscussed fields absent from the output. Never generate placeholder text for unspoken information.
include: Null or empty schema value internally
Omitted field when topic never raised
examples: No blood pressure statement means an empty blood-pressure value.
No family history discussed means family_history remains absent.
counterexamples: Do not write blood pressure not recorded.
Do not write family history not available.
Do not generate normal examination findings.

speaker: patient
caregiver
doctor
documents.purpose: Preserve explicit negation exactly as spoken. Never convert a denied finding into a positive one.
exclude: A positive condition created from a denied condition
examples: Mujhe diabetes nahi hai (I do not have diabetes)
Nange asthma illa (I have no asthma)
counterexamples: Do not record asthma when patient said no asthma.
Do not record chest pain when patient denied it.

speaker: patient
caregiver
doctor
documents.purpose: Preserve the source of every fact. Patient-reported measurements must be distinguishable from clinic-measured values.
exclude: Patient-reported values treated as clinical measurements
counterexamples: Do not mark home glucose reading as clinic-verified.

speaker: patient
caregiver
doctor
documents.purpose: When a speaker explicitly corrects or clarifies an earlier statement, the later statement overrides the earlier one.
exclude: Contradiction without explicit correction treated as confusion
examples: Patient: I said fever since five days, actually it is three days.
counterexamples: Do not treat I have cough and I have cold as a correction.

speaker: patient
caregiver
doctor
documents.purpose: Strictly separate patient-reported history from doctor-ordered plan.
include: Patient or caregiver past and current health information stays in Subjective
Doctor instructions, prescriptions, and orders stay in Plan
exclude: Patient coping strategy as doctor plan
Doctor plan routed to patient history
examples: Patient: I took paracetamol yesterday is history, not prescription.
Doctor: Take paracetamol now is plan, not medication history.
counterexamples: Do not route doctor prescription to current_medications.
Do not route patient OTC use to plan.prescriptions.

speaker: patient
caregiver
doctor
documents.purpose: Never infer a diagnosis from a symptom or combination of symptoms. Only the doctor can supply assessment content.
examples: Fever and cough remain symptoms in Subjective, not a viral diagnosis.
Doctor: This looks like viral fever is an Assessment statement.
counterexamples: Do not write viral fever because patient has fever and cough.
Do not write UTI because patient has burning urination.

speaker: patient
caregiver
documents.purpose: Capture each main reason for the visit with only explicitly spoken details.
include: Normalize slight or slightly as mild, and fluctuating, comes and goes, or on and off as intermittent
exclude: Repeated duration inside the concern name
examples: Cough for one week, worsening for three days.
Mujhe bukhar hai do din se (I have fever for two days).
Thale novu, mild since one week (Headache, mild since one week).
Slight headache which is fluctuating (Headache, mild, intermittent).
counterexamples: Do not include diagnoses like viral fever.
Do not duplicate full illness narrative here.

speaker: patient
caregiver
documents.purpose: Capture the chronological story of the current illness using only patient-reported facts.
include: Home treatment or OTC medicines tried
examples: Patient reports headache for two days and denies vomiting.
Fever started three days ago, on and off. Took paracetamol at home.
Khansi shuru hui ek hafte pahle, raat mein zyada hoti hai (Cough started one week ago, worse at night).
Kempu jaaste illa, nange tale novu matti dizzines ide (No fever, I have headache and dizziness).
counterexamples: Likely viral illness unless the doctor explicitly said it.
Do not create a separate negative-symptom section.

speaker: patient
caregiver
documents.purpose: Capture existing or previous diagnoses, chronic diseases, major illnesses, hospitalizations, surgeries, and explicit denials.
exclude: Current symptom converted into a diagnosis
counterexamples: Do not record asthma when the patient said no asthma.
Do not list current complaints as past medical history.

speaker: patient
caregiver
documents.purpose: Capture medicines the patient was already taking before this consultation, including those prescribed by other doctors. Never capture the doctor's newly prescribed medicines.
include: Duration or length of use when stated
Explicit statement of no current medicines
exclude: Today's new prescription from this doctor
Medicine appearing only in a doctor question
examples: Metformin 500 mg, one tablet every morning.
Patient takes amlodipine 5 mg daily for BP.
Naan daily thyroid tablet thagothini (I take thyroid tablet daily).
counterexamples: Do not place a newly prescribed medicine from today here.
Do not capture a medicine that only appeared in a doctor question.

speaker: patient
caregiver
documents.purpose: Capture explicitly stated drug, food, or other allergies including allergen, type, reaction, severity, and explicit denial.
examples: Mujhe penicillin se allergy hai (I am allergic to penicillin).
Nange yavude medicine allergy illa (I have no medicine allergies).
counterexamples: Do not write no allergies when allergies were not discussed.
Do not record stomach upset as an allergy.

speaker: patient
caregiver
documents.purpose: Capture only explicitly reported health conditions among relatives or an explicit denial of relevant family history.
exclude: Doctor question without a patient or caregiver answer
examples: No family history of heart disease.
counterexamples: Do not infer family history from the patient's diagnosis.
Do not populate this field when family history was not discussed.

speaker: patient
caregiver
documents.purpose: Capture only explicitly reported smoking, tobacco, alcohol, substance use, occupation, exposure, activity, or relevant living conditions.
include: Relevant living conditions or physical activity
Explicit denial of a social-history behavior
exclude: Generic lifestyle advice from the doctor
Doctor question without a patient or caregiver answer
examples: I do not smoke or drink alcohol.
I work in a textile factory.
counterexamples: Do not copy stop smoking advice into social history.
Do not populate this field when social history was not discussed.

speaker: patient
caregiver
doctor
documents.purpose: Capture explicitly supplied measurements with their source. Support individual vital parameters and distinguish patient-reported from clinic-measured values.
include: Temperature with value, unit, and source
Blood pressure with systolic/diastolic, unit, and source
Pulse or heart rate with value and unit
Respiratory rate with value and unit
SpO2 or oxygen saturation with value and unit
Glucose with value, unit, and source
counterexamples: Fever for two days is not a temperature measurement.
Do not write BP 120/80 when it was not measured.
Do not generate weight or BMI from patient appearance.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture only examination findings the doctor explicitly states or observes. Never generate normal findings.
examples: Mild tenderness in right lower quadrant.
counterexamples: Do not write normal examination when no examination occurred.
Do not write chest clear unless the doctor said it.
Do not generate lung fields are clear as default.

speaker: patient
caregiver
doctor
documents.purpose: Capture investigation results that already exist before or during this consultation. Future ordered tests belong in Plan.
exclude: Test ordered today or for future
counterexamples: Order CBC belongs in Plan, not Objective.
Do not generate reference ranges.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture the doctor's explicitly stated overall clinical opinion or interpretation.
examples: Mera impression hai ki ye viral hai (My impression is this is viral).
counterexamples: Do not infer viral illness from fever and cough alone.
Do not generate impression when doctor gave none.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture each diagnosis the doctor explicitly states as likely, suspected, probable, or possible.
examples: Ye shayad viral infection hai (This is probably a viral infection).
counterexamples: Do not upgrade suspected dengue to confirmed dengue.
Do not list symptom alone as provisional diagnosis.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture only diagnoses the doctor explicitly establishes as confirmed or definite.
examples: Ye confirmed diabetes hai (This is confirmed diabetes).
counterexamples: Do not upgrade a suspected condition to confirmed.
Do not infer confirmed status from treatment.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture alternative diagnoses the doctor explicitly considers during the consultation.
counterexamples: Do not create a differential from symptoms alone.
Do not list every possible condition the system knows.
Do not store vague comparison words such as much more as a diagnosis.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture active problems the doctor explicitly addresses or monitors in this consultation.
include: Management status when stated (improving, worsening, stable, uncontrolled)
counterexamples: Do not list every patient complaint automatically.
Do not infer worsening status unless the doctor said it.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture each newly prescribed or modified medication with every explicitly spoken detail. Do not copy patient-reported current medications here.
include: Dosage form when stated (tablet, capsule, syrup, injection)
Specific timing when stated (breakfast, lunch, dinner, morning, noon, night)
Action when stated (START, CONTINUE, CHANGE, STOP, PRN)
examples: Dolo 650 | one tablet | every eight hours | after food | three days | START
Alex syrup | 5 ml | after dinner | five days | START
Continue metformin 500 mg twice daily | CONTINUE
Change amlodipine to 10 mg daily | CHANGE
Paracetamol 500 mg SOS for fever | PRN
counterexamples: Do not fill duration when the doctor did not state it.
Do not copy Metformin from current medications into plan.medications.
Do not invent tablet, capsule, or route.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture tests the doctor orders during this consultation for future completion.
examples: X-ray chest to rule out pneumonia.
counterexamples: Do not place existing results here.
Do not suggest tests the doctor did not order.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture a procedure performed during or planned after this consultation when explicitly stated.
counterexamples: Do not suggest a procedure the doctor did not mention.
Do not list oral medication prescription as a procedure.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture explicit non-medication treatment instructions the doctor gives.
counterexamples: Do not add rest unless the doctor advised it.
Do not place dietary advice here.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture explicit diet, hydration, and lifestyle advice the doctor gives.
examples: Khichdi khaayein aur paani zyada piyein (Eat khichdi and drink more water).
counterexamples: Do not generate hydration advice when not given.
Do not place medication instructions here.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture what the doctor explicitly asks the patient to monitor or track at home.
examples: Check blood sugar fasting every morning.
counterexamples: Do not add monitoring based on diagnosis alone.
Do not place follow-up or warning signs here.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture an explicit referral to another specialty, service, or facility.
examples: Refer to cardiology for evaluation of chest pain.
Refer to higher centre for further management.
counterexamples: Do not create a referral from warning sign instructions.
Do not refer based on symptoms alone.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture when and under what condition the patient should return for review.
examples: Come back in three days if not improving.
Agar aaram nahi hai to do din mein phir se aayein (If not better, come again in two days).
Return earlier if the fever worsens.
counterexamples: Go to emergency for breathing difficulty is a warning sign, not follow-up.
Do not place treatment advice in follow-up.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture the exact warning condition and the required action for seeking earlier or urgent care. Both parts must be preserved independently.
examples: If breathing difficulty develops, go to the hospital immediately.
Agar tez bukhar ho to turant doctor se milein (If high fever develops, see the doctor immediately).
Return earlier if the fever worsens.
counterexamples: Do not rewrite breathing difficulty, go to hospital as just breathing difficulty.
Do not merge warning signs with follow-up.

speaker: doctor
documents.purpose: Capture explicit doctor instructions that genuinely do not fit any other Plan field. This is not a catch-all dumping ground.
exclude: Repeated advice from other Plan fields
examples: Bring previous reports at the next visit.
Carry your prescription whenever you travel.
counterexamples: Do not duplicate diet advice here.
Do not duplicate follow-up or prescriptions here.
